Point 2 of the Assistant Secretary's program policy states that technical assistance will be provided to all Interior bureaus, other federal agencies, states and their local governments, and the private sector in coordinating planning and programming for the development of areas and facilities for the use of off-road vehicles. This is the only place in the program proposal where the private sector is mentioned. We feel that more attention must be given to the private sector in planning for these vehicles. Off-road vehicle programs on private lands can have a significant impact (both beneficial and adverse) on public lands. Perhaps a companion program can be developed to assist the private sector in coping with off-road vehicles.
Point 3 discusses public information. This section should be broadened to include commercial facilities.
The draft statement does not include a discussion on inventory and demand. This is an important part of the broad program policy and should be considered in the final statement. The proposal indicates that each bureau of the Department of the Interior will be charged with locating areas that can stand the development of off-road vehicle facilities and then conceivably these bureaus could proceed with independent development. Executive Order 11644 requires development of a well-coordinated and planned program at the Assistant Secretary's office to get away from a piece-meal approach to public land development.
A statement is made on page 21 that additional resources will be needed to designate areas, develop facilities, post signs and conduct enforcement. This is an important part of program planning but the impact statement does not contain information on how these critical needs will be met.
Because of the growing interest and concern relating to off-road vehicle use public agencies will be required to concentrate more effort on the private sector for satisfying the demand of the more environmentally damaging recreational activities. The multiple use concept of land use has certain advantages where there is a tremendous amount of public land available and where various activities can be segregated for optimum use. In areas where public land is at a premium, the private sector may be the logical place for certain recreational activities.
The off-road vehicles is undoubtedly a permanent addition to the recreational industry. We agree that the opening or closing of all Interior Department lands to off-road vehicle use would be an undesirable solution to the current problem. We support the program policy whereby the Assistant Secretary of the Department of the Interior would be responsible for reviewing and coordinating off-road vehicle use activities on Interior lands.
Thank you for the opportunity to review this draft environmental impact statement.
Very truly yours,
Bureau of Environmental Impact
